title: The Bias Variance Decomposition of Prediction Error
subject: Machine Learning
statement: For squared error regression the expected test error at a point is noise variance plus squared bias plus model variance.
short: Prediction error splits into noise, bias and variance.
long: Prediction error splits into noise, bias and variance. Flexible models lower bias but raise variance.
proof: Expand around the true mean and use independence of noise.
consequence: Explains why minimizing training error can hurt.

title: Empirical Risk Minimization
subject: Machine Learning
statement: ERM selects the hypothesis minimizing average loss on the training sample.
short: Learn by minimizing average training loss.
long: Learn by minimizing average training loss. It replaces unknown expected risk by its empirical estimate.
proof: Define empirical risk as a sample mean and minimize.

title: Optimistic Bias of Training Error
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Training error underestimates test error because the same data selected the hypothesis.
short: A model judged on its own training data looks too good.
long: A model judged on its own training data looks too good. Holdout sets measure the gap.
proof: The minimizing hypothesis has unusually small empirical loss.

title: K Fold Cross Validation
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Split data into k folds, train on the rest and validate on each fold in turn, then average.
short: Rotate the validation fold and average errors.
long: Rotate the validation fold and average errors. Common choices are five and ten folds.
proof: Retrain once per fold and average validation losses.
consequence: Estimates error when data are scarce.

title: Leave One Out Cross Validation
subject: Machine Learning
statement: LOO uses each single observation as a validation set in turn.
short: Validate on one point at a time.
long: Validate on one point at a time. Nearly unbiased but high variance and costly.
proof: Retrain n times omitting one sample.

title: Ridge Regression Closed Form
subject: Machine Learning
statement: L2 penalized least squares has the closed form w equals X transpose X plus lambda I inverse times X transpose y.
short: Ridge shrinks coefficients toward zero.
long: Ridge shrinks coefficients toward zero. The penalty stabilizes ill conditioned fits.
proof: Set the penalized gradient to zero.

title: Lasso Induces Sparsity
subject: Machine Learning
statement: An L1 penalty tends to set some coefficients exactly to zero.
short: L1 regularization performs feature selection.
long: L1 regularization performs feature selection. The L1 ball has corners aligned with axes.
proof: Zero is optimal when correlation with the residual is below lambda.

title: Soft Thresholding for Orthogonal Lasso
subject: Machine Learning
statement: With an orthonormal design the lasso solution soft thresholds ordinary least squares coefficients.
short: Small coefficients become exactly zero.
long: Small coefficients become exactly zero. Separate the objective coordinatewise.
proof: Minimize each quadratic plus absolute value term explicitly.

title: Logistic Regression Model
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Logistic regression models a class probability with a linear score passed through a sigmoid.
short: A linear model with sigmoid output.
long: A linear model with sigmoid output. It is a discriminative probabilistic classifier.
proof: Apply the logistic link to a linear predictor.

title: Logistic Loss Is Convex
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Negative log likelihood of logistic regression is convex in the weights.
short: No spurious local minima exist.
long: No spurious local minima exist. The Hessian is a positive semidefinite weighted Gram matrix.
proof: Compute the Hessian as X transpose D X.
consequence: Gradient methods reach a global optimum.

title: Cross Entropy Is Bernoulli Negative Log Likelihood
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Minimizing binary cross entropy equals maximizing Bernoulli likelihood.
short: Cross entropy is the natural loss for probabilities.
long: Cross entropy is the natural loss for probabilities. Substitute the Bernoulli mass function.
proof: Take logs and negate.

title: Naive Bayes Independence Assumption
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Naive Bayes assumes features are conditionally independent given the class.
short: Pretend features are independent within a class.
long: Pretend features are independent within a class. The assumption is usually false but often harmless.
proof: Apply the chain rule and drop feature dependences.
consequence: Makes high dimensional density estimation easy.

title: Naive Bayes Zero Probability Failure
subject: Machine Learning
statement: An unseen feature value in a class makes the naive Bayes posterior exactly zero.
short: One zero factor erases a class.
long: One zero factor erases a class. Laplace smoothing adds pseudocounts.
proof: A product containing zero vanishes.
consequence: Smoothing is essential for categorical data.

title: K Nearest Neighbors Classifier
subject: Machine Learning
statement: kNN classifies by majority vote among the k closest training points.
short: Let the nearest neighbours vote.
long: Let the nearest neighbours vote. Distance metric and k are key choices.
proof: Compute distances, pick k smallest, take the mode.

title: Cover Hart Consistency of Nearest Neighbors
subject: Machine Learning
statement: If k grows and k over n tends to zero, kNN is asymptotically Bayes optimal under mild conditions.
short: Neighbours eventually win with enough data.
long: Neighbours eventually win with enough data. Bias shrinks as the region shrinks and variance shrinks as it grows.
proof: Balance the two effects using regularity of the distribution.

title: Decision Tree Split by Impurity Reduction
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Trees greedily choose splits that most reduce impurity such as Gini or entropy.
short: Split on the feature separating classes best.
long: Split on the feature separating classes best. Greedy splitting is not globally optimal.
proof: Evaluate candidate splits and keep the largest gain.

title: Gini Impurity
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Gini impurity is the probability of mislabeling a random element under the node distribution.
short: Gini measures class impurity.
long: Gini measures class impurity. It vanishes for pure nodes.
proof: Sum the chance of each label times a different label.

title: Entropy and Information Gain
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Shannon entropy measures label uncertainty and information gain is its reduction after a split.
short: Gain is entropy before minus after.
long: Gain is entropy before minus after. Used by ID3 to choose attributes.
proof: Compute weighted child entropies and subtract.

title: Pruning Combats Tree Overfitting
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Deep trees fit noise so limiting depth or pruning improves test performance.
short: Stop early or cut back branches.
long: Stop early or cut back branches. Pruning trades fit for generalization.
proof: A branch fitted to few examples captures noise.

title: Bootstrap Aggregating
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Bagging trains models on bootstrap resamples and averages predictions.
short: Average models trained on resampled data.
long: Average models trained on resampled data. Helps unstable learners such as trees.
proof: Draw B bootstrap samples and aggregate.
consequence: Improves accuracy of high variance learners.

title: Why Bagging Reduces Variance
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Averaging independent models reduces variance roughly by the number of models.
short: Many independent predictions average out noise.
long: Many independent predictions average out noise. Correlated errors limit the gain.
proof: Use linearity of variance for independent terms.

title: Random Forest
subject: Machine Learning
statement: A random forest averages trees grown on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets at each split.
short: Many decorrelated trees averaged.
long: Many decorrelated trees averaged. Feature subsampling lowers tree correlation.
proof: Grow each tree with rows and feature subsampling.

title: AdaBoost
subject: Machine Learning
statement: AdaBoost reweights misclassified examples and combines weak learners by weighted vote.
short: Focus later learners on hard examples.
long: Focus later learners on hard examples. Each learner sees a reweighted dataset.
proof: Train greedily to reduce exponential loss.
consequence: Turns weak learners into a strong one.

title: AdaBoost Training Error Bound
subject: Machine Learning
statement: If every weak learner has weighted error bounded below one half, AdaBoost training error decays exponentially.
short: Small weak advantages compound.
long: Small weak advantages compound. Bound exponential loss then relate it to zero one error.
proof: Track multiplicative loss decrease per round.

title: Gradient Boosting
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Gradient boosting fits each new model to the negative gradient of the loss at current predictions.
short: Boosting as gradient descent in function space.
long: Boosting as gradient descent in function space. Trees are common weak learners.
proof: Approximate the negative gradient with a base learner.
